# Oracle Unveils New Open-Source Governance Framework For MySQL - Open Source For You

- [News](https://www.opensourceforu.com/category/types-of-content/news/)

## Oracle Unveils New Open-Source Governance Framework For MySQL

*Oracle enters a new phase of MySQL community engagement, launching a formal open-source governance framework to accelerate ecosystem collaboration and code contributions.*

Entering the new phase of MySQL community engagement, Oracle introduced its open-source governance framework. The open-source giant is shifting its community strategy to move beyond basic ecosystem transparency, aiming to accelerate innovation by establishing clear pathways for community participation. The new MySQL Governance Document has been officially published on MySQL.com, joining the existing MySQL Developer Guide as a primary contributor resource.

The introduced governance model defines explicit hierarchical roles, structures, and safety mechanisms to guide the evolution of MySQL:

- Contributors: Can participate by contributing code, testing, writing documentation, reviewing changes, and engaging in technical discussions.
- Committers: Experienced community contributors tasked with reviewing codebase changes and maintaining code quality under the guidance of Mentors.
- Project Leads: Responsible for providing technical leadership over core operational areas of MySQL to secure long-term evolution while validating system performance, stability, and compatibility.
- Administrative Committees: The model includes a Technical Steering Committee alongside a dedicated Vulnerability Group. The Vulnerability Group is explicitly responsible for managing vulnerability reporting, technical security reviews, and coordinated responsible disclosure workflows.

The framework highlights a recent MySQL Contributor Summit, which brought together Oracle engineers and contributors from several competitive and complementary database organisations to collaborate on the future of MySQL. Participating entities included Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud, Percona, ProxySQL, Readyset, VillageSQL, and The MariaDB Foundation.
